messages:
customer-jenny: Hey, getting 502/504s when streaming audio -> hosted inference. Fails after ~30-40s, sometimes immediately. Started ~0900 UTC. No client changes.

luis-support: Sorry for the trouble — can you share a minimal curl and a request-id if available? Also which region?

customer-jenny: curl sample below (we stream via chunked). region=eu1. request-id X-RW-Req: rw-0a1b2c3d 
```
curl -v \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "Content-Type: audio/wav" \n  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \n  --data-binary @audio.wav \n  https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/streaming/infer
```

customer-jenny: we see 502/504 and then the socket closes. no downstream body.

luis-support: Thanks. Can you confirm connection reuse/keepalive? Are you reusing one persistent connection for many streams or new TCP for each?

customer-jenny: persistent across a crowded client pool (node http2 pool). Newer clients use http2 multiplexing. Older clients use TLS keepalive.

infra-bot: auto-alert: increased 5xx rate on eu1 edge gateway (ingress thin-proxy) -> spike at 09:02 UTC, target pool thundering detected.

alex-eng-sre: tagging in. Observed matching 502s from frontdoor -> thin-proxy early-close. Need envoy/nginx upstream logs + trace id span. @luis-support can you grab the raw edge logs for rw-0a1b2c3d timeframe?

luis-support: pulling logs now, got this snippet from thin-proxy: 
```
[2025-07-12T09:02:14.123Z] upstream early close while reading response headers from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api.eu1.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/streaming/infer HTTP/2", upstream: "http://10.20.30.40:8080/", host: "api.eu1.redwood.ai"
```

luis-support: Also saw `upstream response timed out (110: Connection timed out)` for some sessions.

alex-eng-sre: Two hypotheses: 1) backend inference node hitting long GC/block / stuck KV cache refill causing slow headers, causing thin-proxy to early-close; 2) HTTP/2 stream window exhaustion between frontdoor and thin-proxy with head-of-line blocking under heavy multiplexing.

matt-runtime: adding runtime context — we had a low-volume GC regression on one dedicated host, but not fleetwide. However we did flip an experimental keepalive tweak in eu1 thin-proxy yesterday (reduce upstream idle timeout from 75s -> 20s).

alex-eng-sre: That config change would cause exactly this pattern for long streaming requests. If upstream headers take >20s, proxy will close and client sees 502/504.

customer-jenny: ah that matches — streams often take 25-35s before the model returns final chunk.

luis-support: immediate mitigation: we can bump upstream idle timeout for streaming route to 90s and re-enable long keepalive for eu1. Want me to do a config patch and short rolling restart on thin-proxy?

customer-jenny: yes please, that would likely fix it. We can also implement client-side heartbeat if needed.

alex-eng-sre: Agreed. Plan: 1) roll config bump for streaming path (upstream_idle_timeout=90s) on eu1 thin-proxy (canary 5% -> 50% -> 100%), 2) add telemetry to log per-stream backend header latency, 3) follow up with runtime to check for lingering slow nodes.

luis-support: patch created: `edge-config/patches/2025-07-12-eu1-streaming-timeout.json` (canary 5% applied). Will monitor 5xx rate.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary 5% -> eu1 thin-proxy. Audit id: audit-20250712-09-04.

tier2-support: If canary looks good please capture trace spans for rw-0a1b2c3d after 09:10 UTC for confirmation and to correlate to client pool type (http2 vs http1).

alex-eng-sre: Noted — also recommend customers using http2 multiplexing to enable periodic application-level pings (heartbeat frames) to keep streams alive across proxies when long tail is expected.

luis-support: Canary metrics: 5xx rate down by 80% on canary slice after 90s. Rolling to 50% now.

customer-jenny: saw immediate improvement, tests passing in our staging. Thanks all.

matt-runtime: follow-ups: revert the experimental keepalive tweak in eu1, add config guardrails so streaming routes can't get <60s upstream idle by mistake.

alex-eng-sre: closing loop: create postmortem-lite with timeline and config change PR refs. Assigned to @matt-runtime and @luis-support.

customer-jenny: appreciate the fast turn around :thumbsup:
